heading: 13.2 Per-currency dimensions and storage
text:
### 13.2 Per-currency dimensions and storage [LUNI.13.2]

Each currency is a separate `unit dimension`. The base unit is the ISO 4217
minor unit; storage is always `int64`. Minor-unit storage gives exact
integer representation for every routine balance.

| Family | Base unit | dp | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| USD / EUR / GBP / CAD / AUD / CHF / etc. | cent / pence / rappen / … | 2 | Bulk of ISO 4217 |
| JPY / HUF / KRW / IDR / etc. | yen / forint / won / rupiah | 0 | No minor unit in ISO 4217 |
| KWD / JOD / BHD / LYD / etc. | fils / qirsh / … | 3 | Gulf dinars |
| Sub-currency precision (pip, equity 4dp) | `<ccy>_pip`, `<ccy>_4dp` | 4–8 | Each precision is its own dimension |

Sub-minor precision is a *separate* `unit dimension` per currency — `currency_usd_4dp`
(pip-precision USD) is distinct from `currency_usd`. Conversion within a single
currency (`USD_dollar` ↔ `USD_cent` ↔ `USD_pip`) is exact tier-1 affine
(`unit <sym>: ... = <power_of_10>`). Cross-currency conversion always goes
through `unit fx_pair`.

Per-currency dimensions are never interchangeable for arithmetic — `currency_usd +
currency_eur` is a compile error ([LUNI.8.2] cross-dimension). To add them, the
author explicitly converts one side via `unit fx_pair` and `.round("<mode>")`.
